title: Reedy realization transfers combinatorial prism homotopies
statement: Use the simplicial model-category, simplicial tensor, Reedy model-structure, simplex-category, and combinatorial simplicial-homotopy notions of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization], [def-coef-simplicial-tensor-cotensor], [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure], [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], and [lem-coef-simplicial-extra-degeneracy-prism]. Let $\mathcal M$ be a simplicial model category and let $X_\bullet,Y_\bullet:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal M$ be Reedy-cofibrant. For any simplicial object $Z_\bullet$ define its tensor realization by $$|Z_\bullet|=\operatorname{coeq}\left(\coprod_{\alpha:[m]\to[n]} Z_n\otimes\Delta^m\rightrightarrows\coprod_{n\geq0}Z_n\otimes\Delta^n\right),$$ where $\Delta^n=\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta(-,[n])$, and the parallel arrows use $Z(\alpha)$ and $\Delta^\alpha$, respectively. Then $|X_\bullet|$ is cofibrant, and $P_X=|X_\bullet|\otimes\Delta^1$, with vertex maps $i_0,i_1:|X_\bullet|\to P_X$ and projection $p:P_X\to |X_\bullet|$ induced by $\Delta^1\to\Delta^0$, is a cylinder object: $p i_0=p i_1=1$, $p$ is a weak equivalence, and $i_0\amalg i_1:|X_\bullet|\amalg|X_\bullet|\to P_X$ is a cofibration. For maps $u,v:X_\bullet\to Y_\bullet$, every combinatorial simplicial homotopy from $u$ to $v$ induces a map $\widetilde H:P_X\to |Y_\bullet|$ with $\widetilde H i_0=|u|$ and $\widetilde H i_1=|v|$. Tensor notation $Z\otimes K$ denotes the chosen tensor $K\otimes Z$.

source.place: Dugger, A Primer on Homotopy Colimits, formula (3.2), printed p.9; skeletal pushout in the proof of Theorem 3.5, printed pp.10-11; Section 19.1, printed p.90. Read online on 2026-10-17; not archived. These give the coend and the cofibrancy method, not the exact combinatorial-prism theorem. The prism formulation is agent-written; no Stacks tag states it.

proof.text: First translate the mapping-space version of the simplicial axiom into the needed pushout-product assertion. For $i:A\to B$ in $\mathcal M$ and $j:K\to L$ in simplicial sets, lifts from $(A\otimes L)\amalg_{A\otimes K}(B\otimes K)\to B\otimes L$ against $q:E\to F$ correspond, by the tensor adjunction, to lifts of $j$ against $\operatorname{Map}(B,E)\to\operatorname{Map}(A,E)\times_{\operatorname{Map}(A,F)}\operatorname{Map}(B,F)$. If $i,j$ are cofibrations and $q$ a trivial fibration, the latter map is a trivial Kan fibration, hence such lifts exist. If $i$ or $j$ is trivial, the same argument works for every fibration $q$: in the first case the mapping-space map is trivial, in the second case $j$ lifts against any Kan fibration. The defining lifting classes of the two model weak factorization systems therefore make the pushout product a cofibration, trivial in either of these cases. This is only an adjunction of lifting squares, with no cofibrancy assumption on $A$ or $B$.

source.place: Section 19.1, printed p.90; elementary adjunction-of-lifting-squares derivation of the pushout-product formulation from the cited mapping-space axiom.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-tensor-coend-skeletal-pushouts] in $\mathcal M$. It gives $R_{-1}=0$, the sequence $R_n$, the specified pushout squares with attaching maps $B_n\to X_n\otimes\Delta^n$, and $\operatorname{colim}R_n\cong|X|$. The latching diagram in that statement is exactly the direct latching diagram for $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$. Reedy cofibrancy of $X$ thus makes $L_nX\to X_n$ a cofibration. By the Kan-model node the boundary inclusion $\partial\Delta^n\to\Delta^n$ is a cofibration, since it is degreewise injective. Step 1 says that $B_n\to X_n\otimes\Delta^n$ is their pushout-product cofibration, including $n=0$ where both latching and boundary objects are initial.

source.place: Formula (3.2) and the proof of Theorem 3.5, printed pp.9-10; categorical skeletal formula supplied by the cited supporting node.

proof.text: The pushout-closure statement of [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure], applied to the left class of ground trivial fibrations, makes every $R_{n-1}\to R_n$ a cofibration. To pass to the countable colimit without assuming that weak equivalences preserve colimits, apply [lem-coef-small-direct-colimit-lifting] to the category $\mathbf N$ with its order, the constant initial diagram, and the diagram $n\mapsto R_n$. Take $T$ to be the class of trivial fibrations. At $n=0$ the relative latching map is $0\to R_0$; for $n>0$ the predecessor category has terminal object $n-1$, so that map is $R_{n-1}\to R_n$. These maps are precisely the cofibrations just established. The indexing category is small and every nonidentity arrow strictly increases degree. The cited statement gives $0\to\operatorname{colim}R_n$ in the same left class, hence a cofibration. Using Step 2 identifies its codomain with $|X|$, proving the cofibrancy assertion.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 3.5, printed pp.10-11, with the countable passage justified by the existing general direct-colimit lifting theorem.

proof.text: Put $A=|X|$. The endpoint inclusion $e_0:\Delta^0\to\Delta^1$ is a one-dimensional horn inclusion, so it has the left lifting property against all Kan fibrations. The Kan-model weak factorization system makes it a trivial cofibration. Apply Step 1 with $0\to A$: its pushout product with $e_0$ is $i_0:A\cong A\otimes\Delta^0\to A\otimes\Delta^1$, hence a weak equivalence. The tensor representing isomorphism identifies $A\otimes\Delta^0$ with $A$, and functoriality gives $pi_0=pi_1=1_A$. Two-out-of-three now gives $p$ a weak equivalence. Finally $\partial\Delta^1=\Delta^0\amalg\Delta^0\to\Delta^1$ is a monomorphism; Step 1 with $0\to A$ identifies its pushout product with $i_0\amalg i_1:A\amalg A\to A\otimes\Delta^1$ and makes it a cofibration. This proves all cylinder properties. No fibrancy is used.

source.place: Section 19.1, printed p.90; endpoint horn and two-out-of-three argument, rather than applying the pushout-product axiom to the non-cofibration interval collapse.

proof.text: Let $q_r:Y_r\otimes\Delta^r\to|Y|$ be the coend maps, and write $H_j^n:X_n\to Y_{n+1}$ for the given prism data. Switch the factors in the explicit $\sigma_j$ of [lem-coef-infinity-right-prism-boundary] to obtain $\kappa_j:\Delta^{n+1}\to\Delta^n\times\Delta^1$ with vertices $(0,0),\ldots,(j,0),(j,1),\ldots,(n,1)$. These simplices cover the product: a monotone chain in $[n]\times[1]$ lies in one of them by choosing $j$ between its last lower coordinate and first upper coordinate (use $j=0$ or $n$ for a chain entirely in one end). On $X_n\otimes\Delta^{n+1}$ assign $g_j=q_{n+1}(H_j^n\otimes1)$. Adjacent simplices meet along the face omitting position $j+1$ in each. On this face the coend relation turns the two restrictions into $q_n(d_{j+1}H_j^n\otimes1)$ and $q_n(d_{j+1}H_{j+1}^n\otimes1)$, equal by the middle prism identity. For $j<k$ their common vertices are $(0,0),\ldots,(j,0),(k,1),\ldots,(n,1)$, a face contained in every intervening adjacent intersection. Consequently all pairwise restrictions agree. The product is the degreewise union of these simplicial subsets, so its union colimit and the tensor universal property glue the $g_j$ to $F_n:X_n\otimes(\Delta^n\times\Delta^1)\to|Y|$. Tensoring in the simplicial-set parameter preserves this colimit since maps out correspond to simplicial maps into $\operatorname{Map}(X_n,-)$.

source.place: Lemma 3.1.2.12 and proof, explicit sigma maps; agent calculation of intersections and gluing using the given combinatorial prism identities.

proof.text: The $F_n$ respect every coend relation; here are the generator checks. For a coface $\delta_i:[n-1]\to[n]$ and $0\leq j<n$, the map $(\delta_i\times1)\kappa_j$ is $\kappa_{j+1}\delta_i$ if $i\leq j$ and $\kappa_j\delta_{i+1}$ if $i>j$, by their vertex lists. The required equalities of maps to $|Y|$ are respectively $d_iH_{j+1}^n=H_j^{n-1}d_i$ and $d_{i+1}H_j^n=H_j^{n-1}d_i$, exactly the two strict-inequality face identities. For a codegeneracy $\sigma_i:[n+1]\to[n]$ and $0\leq j\leq n+1$, $(\sigma_i\times1)\kappa_j$ is $\kappa_{j-1}\sigma_i$ when $i<j$, and $\kappa_j\sigma_{i+1}$ when $i\geq j$. Compatibility is therefore $s_iH_{j-1}^n=H_j^{n+1}s_i$ and $s_{i+1}H_j^n=H_j^{n+1}s_i$, the two degeneracy identities. After composing with $q$, the coend relations of $Y$ convert these identities into $F_n(1\otimes(\Delta^\alpha\times1))=F_m(X(\alpha)\otimes1)$ for the corresponding $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$. Every order-preserving map is a composite of cofaces and codegeneracies (factor it into a surjection and an injection and delete repetitions or missing vertices), so the equality holds for every $\alpha$.

source.place: Lines 48-67, the precise face and degeneracy identities; explicit vertex checks and their translation by the realization coend relation.

proof.text: Step 6 supplies a map from $\int^n X_n\otimes(\Delta^n\times\Delta^1)$ to $|Y|$. This coend is canonically $|X|\otimes\Delta^1$. Indeed, for objects $B,T$ and simplicial sets $L,K$, the tensor adjunctions identify maps $(B\otimes L)\otimes K\to T$ and $B\otimes(L\times K)\to T$ with maps $L\times K\to\operatorname{Map}(B,T)$; the mutually inverse representing maps give a natural isomorphism of these tensors. Also $-\otimes K$ is left adjoint to the cotensor $(-)^K$, so maps from the tensor of a coproduct or coequalizer to $T$ are precisely the compatible families of maps from the tensors of its summands. This directly proves preservation of the coproducts and coequalizer defining $|X|$. Apply these facts with $K=\Delta^1$ to identify the two coequalizers, summand by summand. The obtained map is the required $\widetilde H:P_X\to|Y|$.

source.place: Formula (3.2) and Section 19.1: explicit representing-isomorphism and coequalizer universal-property calculation.

proof.text: The all-zero end of $\Delta^n\times\Delta^1$ is the last face of $\kappa_n$, so $F_n$ restricts there to $q_n(d_{n+1}H_n^n\otimes1)=q_n(u_n\otimes1)$. The all-one end is the zeroth face of $\kappa_0$, giving $q_n(d_0H_0^n\otimes1)=q_n(v_n\otimes1)$. The two face equalities are exactly the endpoint identities of the given combinatorial homotopy. Under the summandwise isomorphism of Step 7, these restrictions are composition with $i_0$ and $i_1$. Thus the coequalizer universal property gives $\widetilde H i_0=|u|$ and $\widetilde H i_1=|v|$. The argument did not require $Y$ to be cofibrant, and in particular applies to the Reedy-cofibrant $Y$ assumed in the item.

source.place: Lines 55-56, endpoint identities; agent verification of the corresponding all-zero and all-one prism faces.
